description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of three LLaMA-2 models—LLaMA-2-7B, LLaMA-2-13B, and LLaMA-2-70B—on the CoLeG-E benchmark, measured as percentage accuracy, under four different fine-tuning conditions: no SFT (supervised fine-tuning), SFT on dataset D₀, SFT on datasets D₀ and D₁, and SFT on datasets D₀, D₁, and D₂. The vertical axis represents CoLeG-E (%) ranging from 0 to 50, with tick marks at intervals of 10. The horizontal axis lists the three model sizes. For each model, four bars are grouped together, distinguished by color and pattern: light blue with diagonal stripes for “no SFT,” light orange with horizontal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀,” light purple with diagonal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀, D₁,” and light red with horizontal stripes for “+ SFT on D₀, D₁, D₂.” Performance consistently increases with the number of fine-tuned datasets across all models. For LLaMA-2-7B, scores rise from ~4% (no SFT) to ~20% (D₀), ~28% (D₀,D₁), and ~30% (D₀,D₁,D₂). For LLaMA-2-13B, scores increase from ~8% to ~32%, ~36%, and ~38%. For LLaMA-2-70B, scores climb from ~26% to ~46%, ~50%, and ~51%. The chart visually demonstrates that both model scale and the breadth of fine-tuning data contribute to improved performance on longer math word problems.
